clue.text: Corrupt chairman's lack of respect for rules

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or perverted, so the letters of the following word are put into a twisted new order

explanation.surface: A crooked chairman shows contempt for the regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' reads as an adjective describing the chairman but signals an anagram of CHAIRMANS, the possessive S included.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchism rejects government and imposed order, so it is a disregard for laws.

clue.text: Accomplished over mile in walk

indicators.note: in a down clue one word placed over another can straddle it, so here the first word encloses the second

parts.note: an accomplished person is able

explanation.surface: An accomplished athlete covers a mile on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs for a slow, leisurely stroll.

clue.text: Aggressive type mentioned in a hymn book

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken out, so the solver listens to how the phrase is pronounced

parts.note: a psalter is a book of psalms used in worship

explanation.surface: Someone violent turns up named in a book of hymns.
explanation.walkthrough: The P of 'psalter' is silent, so 'a psalter' is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An attacker is someone who commits violence on another person.

clue.text: Monument, aptly, one put up in church

indicators.note: in places the turned-up pieces inside the letters for church
in a down clue putting something up turns it bottom to top, so the pair is read backwards

parts.note: pat as an adverb means aptly or fittingly
taken as written

explanation.surface: A memorial, fittingly, is raised in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aptly' looks like a comment on the surface but gives PAT; 'put up' turns PAT plus ONE upward, giving ENOTAP, and 'in' sets that inside the church abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a war memorial honouring the dead buried elsewhere, such as the one in Whitehall.

clue.text: Second judge ignored suspect

indicators.note: ignored means left out, so the letter for judge is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: a jiffy is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A deputy judge disregarded the suspect in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second judge' looks like a deputy on the bench; 'Second' is JIFFY and 'ignored' drops J.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean dubious, doubtful or not to be trusted.

clue.text: Man with wind makes you bridle partly

parts.note: Martin is a man's name
a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: A man in a windy spot reins in his horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A martingale is a strap in a horse's harness, a component of the tack fixed to the bridle or reins.

clue.text: Is bouncing back, having fresh strength

indicators.note: something bouncing back comes the other way, so the word is turned round

parts.note: fresh means new

explanation.surface: Someone recovering after a setback, full of renewed vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew is muscle and tendon, used figuratively for physical power.

clue.text: Former army caterer redeployed in Ulster

indicators.note: redeployed means rearranged, as troops are, so the letters of the place name are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An old army supplier is posted again to Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster, Northern Ireland, saw British army deployments, so 'redeployed' fits the surface but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A sutler was a trader who followed an army selling provisions to soldiers.

clue.text: Woman's written up article, omitting almost half

indicators.note: in a down clue words written upward read backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: almost half means a little under half of the word's letters, taken from its front

explanation.surface: A woman's article is printed, with nearly half of it cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' turns AN into NA; 'almost half' takes OMI, three of the eight letters of 'omitting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a female first name, Ruth's mother-in-law in the Bible.

clue.text: Saw single broken container

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the letters of the two words are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone spotted one shattered vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' reads as the past of see, but it is just letters for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking glass holds wine, so it is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Animal, black one seen with offspring

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
I is the Roman numeral for one
a son is offspring

explanation.surface: A dark beast is spotted with its young.
explanation.definitionFit: A bison is a large wild ox, a type of beast.

clue.text: Snowdrift affected US team's progress towards goal

indicators.note: affected means altered or acted upon, so the letters of the word are changed in order

explanation.surface: A drift of snow held up an American football side.
explanation.walkthrough: In American football a team gains a first down by advancing ten yards, earning a fresh set of attempts.
explanation.definitionFit: In gridiron, achieving ten yards of advance toward the end zone renews the attempts.

clue.text: What's fair value of shares?

explanation.surface: Someone asks what shares are really worth.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairness or impartiality, and the shareholders' stake in a company.

clue.text: Doing some metalwork is fascinating

explanation.surface: Working with metal turns out to be gripping.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixing plates with bolts hammered flat, and gripping or enthralling.

clue.text: Prior disturbance, military police will be brought in to protect citizen

indicators.note: prior means coming before, so the covered piece is placed ahead of the disturbance
brought in means taken inside, so the police abbreviation goes inside the word for protect

parts.note: to coat something is to cover and protect it
a riot is a public disturbance

explanation.surface: Police are called to guard a citizen before an earlier riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior' reads as an adjective on 'disturbance' but tells you the protected, police-filled piece comes first; 'will be brought in' signals the insertion and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A compatriot is a fellow countryman, someone from the same nation.

clue.text: Misbehave and ruin part of golf course

parts.note: to cut up something is to damage or wreck it
the rough is the long grass beside a fairway

explanation.surface: A golfer behaves badly, tearing up the turf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut up rough' is British slang for becoming angry or troublesome.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming aggressive or difficult is a way of behaving badly.

clue.text: Large birds of prey arrive in South American capital

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the name of the city

parts.note: Caracas is the capital of Venezuela
AR is the timetable abbreviation for arrive or arrival

explanation.surface: Big raptors fly into a Venezuelan city.
explanation.definitionFit: Caracaras are large falcons of the Americas.

clue.text: Great Eastern states

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for Maine, an eastern US state
GA is the postal abbreviation for Georgia, another eastern US state

explanation.surface: The eastern seaboard is magnificent.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is informal for huge or excellent.

clue.text: In French clubs woman introduces a spicy snack

parts.note: en is French for in
C is the card abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: a woman introduces something by bringing it in, so the letter goes inside her name

parts.note: Hilda is a woman's name

explanation.surface: At French nightclubs a woman brings in a hot bite to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican tortilla rolled round a filling with chilli sauce.

clue.text: Work land inside vile fortified prison

indicators.note: inside puts the farming word within the word for vile

parts.note: base means low and vile
to till is to cultivate soil

explanation.surface: Prisoners labour in fields within a grim fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the Paris jail stormed in 1789, a fortress used to hold prisoners.

clue.text: Repeatedly told to use oars in one type of boat

indicators.note: repeatedly means done twice or more, so the piece appears two times
told means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to row is to use oars

explanation.surface: Someone is told again and again to start rowing.
explanation.walkthrough: A ro-ro is a roll-on roll-off ferry for vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Ro-ro ferries let vehicles drive on and off, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Gadgets created initially by Scotsman to cut fruit

indicators.note: to cut means to slice into, so the pieces go inside the word for fruit

parts.note: apples are fruit
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A Scot invents devices for slicing fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: IAN and C (first of 'created') go into APPLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Appliances are devices or machines, such as kitchen equipment.

clue.text: Make enquiries about diamonds being expensive

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the snooping word goes round the gems

parts.note: to pry is to inquire nosily
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone asks around about costly gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean costly or dear.

clue.text: Famous person with no stomach for speed

indicators.note: the stomach is the middle of the body, so the central letter is removed

parts.note: a celebrity is a famous person

explanation.surface: A star with no appetite wants things done fast.
explanation.walkthrough: B is the fifth of nine letters in CELEBRITY, its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Celerity is swiftness or quickness of movement.

clue.text: Left port with cargo on board

parts.note: Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A ship departs harbour fully loaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means loaded, carrying a heavy burden.

clue.text: Flight in first airship

indicators.note: in shows the answer is contained within the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A trip aboard the first dirigible.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a set of steps between floors.

clue.text: Leader making shock announcement

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken out, so the word is heard

parts.note: to shock is to shake someone up

explanation.surface: A ruler declares something startling.
explanation.walkthrough: Many speakers pronounce the Arab title to rhyme with 'make'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheik is an Arab chief or ruler.

clue.text: From Christian names select suitable one for daughter

indicators.note: from shows the answer is taken out of the letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Parents choose a fitting Christian name for their baby girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna is a girl's name, a fitting choice for a daughter.

clue.text: Row about editor making cut

indicators.note: about means around, so the quarrel word surrounds the editor

parts.note: a ruction is a row or noisy argument

explanation.surface: An argument over the editor making cuts to a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' rhymes with cow here, a quarrel, not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduction is a decrease, a lessening.

clue.text: I beg you, take penny off rent

indicators.note: take and off together mean to remove, so the coin letter is dropped from the begging word
with take this signals removing the letter

parts.note: please is a polite plea

explanation.surface: A tenant pleads for a little off the rent.
explanation.definitionFit: To lease is to rent out property under contract.

clue.text: Cheerful group of students returning to New York

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the union's letters are read backwards

parts.note: the NUS is Britain's National Union of Students

explanation.surface: Students head back to New York in high spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunny disposition is bright and happy.

clue.text: Painting taken round the country has no new distinguishing feature

indicators.note: taken round means turned about, so the word is reversed

parts.note: painting is art

indicators.note: has no means lacking, so the letter for new is removed

parts.note: Denmark is a country

explanation.surface: A touring art exhibition lacks anything novel to mark it out.
explanation.walkthrough: ART reversed is TRA; DENMARK without N gives DEMARK.
explanation.definitionFit: A trademark is a characteristic mark or habit someone is known by.
